formIdentityNote: Three official forms, no invention. The petition is the state's own model for this exact section, revised February 2022 and used as published. The ORDER is the state's model for THREE sections at once — §§ 411.0725, 411.073 and 411.0735 — and it is the SAME BINARY, by SHA-256, that the sibling § 411.0735 family binds; this family pins its own entry for it and records the whole file's digest here, so its binding is legible without reading any other family's. The court indicates which section applies by marking one of three boxes on the order's page 2, and that box is refused as court-owned even though this family is unambiguously the § 411.0725 route, because the sentence above it records a judicial FINDING. The Statement of Inability is the statewide bilingual form the Supreme Court of Texas approved in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, held in the human_source_returns custody rather than the Master Library; the receipt records which custody supplied the bytes rather than assuming.
whatThisReceiptDoesNotEstablish: that any output is approved for participant delivery

whether the participant qualifies for the AUTOMATIC order under § 411.072 instead, which is nearly free and requires no petition; the committed record carries that as a point where self-help ends and the packet says so before it says anything about filing

what a given Texas county's civil filing fee actually is — § 411.0745(b) sets the type of fee and not an amount, county schedules govern, and the registry carries the figure as an unresolved question with impact release_blocker

whether the county the participant files in expects proof that the district attorney received a copy; § 411.0745(e) makes the court responsible for notice and OCA instructions direct the proof, so the component ships conditional

which of the three § 411.0725 waiting periods applies, because that is decided by the grade and Penal Code chapter of the participant's own offence and by the date of the discharge and dismissal — none of which the platform has seen
which of the five § 411.072 disqualifications in paragraph 2 applies to the participant
whether the participant's county requires the petition to be notarized — Subchapter E-1 does not, and county practice may differ

that the bound OCA forms carry a current revision: the registry records, as an unresolved question with impact release_blocker, that the OCA models carry a February 2022 revision and have not been revised for the 2023 recodification of expunction into Chapter 55A
